The checks for `accept`, sizes, counts and `validate` run in the browser only, to tell people early why a file was left out. Anyone can skip them, so check every upload again on your server.

The drop zone isn’t a control, so always keep a trigger beside it for people who use a keyboard or a screen reader. The list is one tab stop, and each remove button is named for its file, like “Remove photo.png”, and stays out of the tab order because Delete on the item does the same.

The file input holds the files people choose, drop or paste, and submits them with a form. Uploading them is up to your app. `FileInputItem` with no children renders a finished row with a preview, the name, the size and a remove button, once for each file in the list.
The layout: list, grid or chips. Items carry it too.
The variant: default, composer or overlay.
Upload button
What screen readers hear after a change.
With `target="document"` and `variant="overlay"`, the zone covers the page while files are dragged over the window, and takes files dropped anywhere. A drop on another zone stays with that zone.

With `variant="composer"`, the drop zone is the card around a message box, and `layout="chips"` lists files as compact chips. `pasteTarget` takes pasted screenshots from the text area, while pasted text stays text.
With a `name`, the files submit through a native file input, even before the page hydrates. Rejected files never submit, and a form reset empties the list.
`FileInputItemPreview` shows an image from an object URL it revokes when the file goes away, and an icon for other types. With `layout="grid"`, each file is a square tile.

`accept` takes MIME types, wildcards and extensions. `maxFiles`, `minSize` and `maxSize` set the limits, and `validate` adds checks of your own. `FileInputRejections` lists each file that was left out with every reason, until the next accepted file.
`directory` picks a whole folder and turns on `multiple`. Item names show the path inside the folder.
`invalid` marks the drop zone and the trigger, and the trigger tells screen readers. Point the trigger’s `aria-describedby` at your message.
details has the reason and the added, removed and rejected files.
image for an image preview, icon for an icon by file type.
